narrative: The model estimated an 81% probability that you would be a bad credit risk, so your application was denied. This means that, based on the profile supplied, repayment problems were judged substantially more likely than not. The strongest factor was the requested credit duration: you asked for 60 months, far longer than the approved applicants’ average of about 19 months. A longer commitment increased the perceived risk. The second most influential factor was your checking-account status: a balance of 0–200 DM was treated as riskier than the most common approved pattern of no/unknown balance, and it pushed the decision toward denial. Third, your property information was recorded as unknown/none. Because only 7.8% of approved applicants had this profile, the absence of documented property or assets added further weight toward bad credit. Other details, such as the requested amount being above the approved average, may also have contributed, but the three factors above were the main drivers. To improve your chances next time, consider requesting a shorter and smaller loan, building a stronger checking-account balance and savings record, and providing documented assets, collateral, or a guarantor. You could also ask the bank what specific evidence would strengthen a future application before reapplying.
